statement: A unique index targeted by a PostgREST/supabase-js `.upsert(row, { onConflict: '<columns>' })` call must be a FULL, non-partial index on exactly those columns — Postgres cannot resolve a column-list `ON CONFLICT` clause against an index carrying a `WHERE` predicate, and this fails only at live execution (`no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification`), never inside an in-memory/fake Supabase client. When a column may legitimately be absent, rely on Postgres's own NULL-uniqueness semantics (an ordinary unique index already allows unlimited NULLs) rather than reaching for a partial predicate to achieve the same effect.

canaries.assertion: 'the exact PostgREST-generated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, draft_idempotency_key) DO NOTHING succeeds' against the corrected non-partial index, AND 'REGRESSION GUARD: the SAME statement against the OLD PARTIAL index fails with the exact reported Postgres error' — reproduces `no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification` verbatim against a real local Postgres 16 instance, run via `npm run test:integration`.

Application-level resume/supersede logic (createOrResumeDraft, claimDraftForPreflight) against a fake Supabase client — documents in its own header that it covers ONLY this layer and explicitly defers the Postgres ON CONFLICT/partial-index guarantee to the real-Postgres integration test above, rather than implying fake-client coverage is sufficient.

occurrences.defect: uq_token_launches_draft_idempotency was created as a PARTIAL unique index (`WHERE draft_idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`); createOrResumeDraft's `.upsert(row, { onConflict: 'tenant_id,draft_idempotency_key', ignoreDuplicates: true })` would have failed at live execution with 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification'. Caught on operator review before the migration reached live Supabase; never actually failed in production.

notes: Single occurrence so far — held at `candidate`, not `validated`, per this registry's own rule (validated requires >= 2 occurrences or the milestone-close check refuses it). The next agent who reaches for a partial unique index as an `onConflict` target anywhere in this codebase (or anyone adding a new upsert-based idempotency key to any other table) should record a second occurrence here rather than rediscovering this from scratch.

The general shape generalizes beyond Bankr/token_launches: ANY table in this codebase that adds an idempotency-key-style unique column intended for `.upsert(..., { onConflict, ignoreDuplicates: true })` use should default to a non-partial unique index and rely on NULL-uniqueness semantics for 'this column doesn't apply to every row', never a `WHERE <col> IS NOT NULL` predicate on the index the upsert targets.

Distinguish carefully from `uq_token_launches_current` in this same migration, which IS a partial index (`WHERE superseded_by IS NULL`) and is correctly left that way — it is never targeted by an `onConflict` upsert (application logic reads it via an explicit SELECT and decides resume/create/supersede itself), so its partial predicate is not a PostgREST inference problem. The rule this candidate states is about INDEXES TARGETED BY onConflict specifically, not about partial indexes in general — a partial index used only as a plain DB-level constraint backstop (checked via ordinary INSERT, whose unique-violation error is caught and handled) remains a perfectly good pattern.
